headers.description: Optional headers to send with the request as a dictionary of header values.

Content-Type.description: The media type of the resource being requested, typically 'application/json'.

Authorization.description: The credentials to authenticate a user agent with a server, typically formatted as 'Bearer {token}'.

timeout.description: The maximum amount of time to wait for a response from the server, in seconds. A longer timeout may be necessary for slower network connections or overloaded servers. This is a float type value.

params.description: URL parameters to append to the URL. Sent as a dictionary of key-value pairs.

query.description: The query parameter for search or filtering.

page.description: The page number parameter for pagination. Used to retrieve a specific page of results.

auth.description: HTTP authentication credentials formatted as a (username, password) tuple.

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem), if required for the request.

cookies.description: Cookies to send with the request as a dictionary of cookie names and values.

sessionid.description: Session identifier cookie, used to recognize client sessions on the server.

csrftoken.description: CSRF protection token cookie, used to prevent cross-site request forgery attacks.

proxies.description: Proxy settings as a dictionary, mapping protocol or protocol and hostname to the URL of the proxy.

http.description: Proxy URL to use for HTTP requests, including the port number.

https.description: Proxy URL to use for HTTPS requests, including the port number.

stream.description: Whether to stream the download of the response. If False, the response content will be immediately downloaded. Streaming is useful for handling large files or responses.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not. Set to False to skip certificate verification, which is not recommended unless you are sure of the server's identity.

message.content:
Below is a quick‑start guide for building (or using) an API that accepts an IP address and returns company‑level data—including contact information when it exists. I’ll cover: | What you need | Options | Notes | |----------------|---------|-------| | **IP → Company lookup** | • **ipinfo.io**
• **ipstack.com**
• **ipapi.co**
• **ipwhois.io**
• **ipgeolocation.io** | All offer “organization” fields; some also expose phone/email. | | **Free tier** | ipinfo.io (50k/month), ipapi.co (1k/month), ipwhois.io (1k/month) | Good for prototyping. | | **Paid tier** | ipinfo.io (10k+), ipstack (10k+), ipapi.co (10k+), ipwhois.io (10k+), ipgeolocation.io (10k+) | Higher rate limits, more fields, SLA. | | **Self‑hosted** | **MaxMind GeoIP2 / GeoLite2** + **IP2Location LITE** | No API key, but you need to parse CSV/DB. | | **Privacy** | GDPR & CCPA compliance varies; check each provider’s policy. | | --- ## 1. Quick‑start with **ipinfo.io** ### 1.1 Sign up & get an API token ```bash curl -X POST https://ipinfo.io/api/v1/token \ -d "email=you@example.com" \ -d "password=yourpassword" ``` You’ll receive a token like `1234567890abcdef`. ### 1.2 API call ```http GET https://ipinfo.io//json?token=YOUR_TOKEN ``` #### Example (Python) ```python import requests def get_company_info(ip, token): url = f"https://ipinfo.io/{ip}/json" params = {"token": token} resp = requests.get(url, params=params, timeout=5) resp.raise_for_status() data = resp.json() # Extract fields company = data.get("org") # e.g., "AS15169 Google LLC" city = data.get("city") region = data.get("region") country= data.get("country") postal = data.get("postal") loc = data.get("loc") # "lat,lon" # ipinfo.io does NOT return phone/email in the free tier. # Paid tier adds "phone" and "email" under "company" key. return { "company": company, "city": city, "region": region, "country": country, "postal": postal, "location": loc, } # Usage token = "YOUR_TOKEN" print(get_company_info("8.8.8.8", token)) ``` ### 1.3 Response format (free tier) ```json { "ip": "8.8.8.8", "hostname": "dns.google", "city": "Mountain View", "region": "California", "country": "US", "loc": "37.3860,-122.0840", "org": "AS15169 Google LLC", "postal": "94035", "timezone": "America/Los_Angeles", "readme": "https://ipinfo.io/missingauth" } ``` Paid tier adds: ```json "company": { "name": "Google LLC", "phone": "+1-650-253-0000", "email": "support@google.com", "website": "https://www.google.com" } ``` --- ## 2. Quick‑start with **ipapi.co** ### 2.1 API call ```http GET https://ipapi.co//json/?key=YOUR_KEY ``` #### Example (Python) ```python def get_ipapi_info(ip, key): url = f"https://ipapi.co/{ip}/json/" params = {"key": key} r = requests.get(url, params=params, timeout=5) r.raise_for_status() data = r.json() return { "ip": data.get("ip"), "city": data.get("city"), "region": data.get("region"), "country": data.get("country_name"), "postal": data.get("postal"), "latitude": data.get("latitude"), "longitude": data.get("longitude"), "org": data.get("org"), "domain": data.get("domain"), "asn": data.get("asn"), "timezone": data.get("timezone"), # Paid tier: "contact" object } ``` Paid tier returns: ```json "contact": { "name": "Google LLC", "phone": "+1-650-253-0000", "email": "support@google.com", "website": "https://www.google.com" } ``` --- ## 3. Quick‑start with **ipwhois.io** ### 3.1 API call ```http GET https://ipwhois.app/json/?key=YOUR_KEY ``` #### Example (Python) ```python def get_ipwhois_info(ip, key): url = f"https://ipwhois.app/json/{ip}" params = {"key": key} r = requests.get(url, params=params, timeout=5) r.raise_for_status() data = r.json() return { "ip": data.get("ip"), "city": data.get("city"), "region": data.get("region"), "country": data.get("country"), "postal": data.get("postal"), "latitude": data.get("latitude"), "longitude": data.get("longitude"), "org": data.get("org"), "isp": data.get("isp"), "domain": data.get("domain"), "timezone": data.get("timezone"), # Paid tier: "contact" object } ``` Paid tier adds: ```json "contact": { "name": "Google LLC", "phone": "+1-650-253-0000", "email": "support@google.com", "website": "https://www.google.com" } ``` --- ## 4. Self‑hosted alternative: **MaxMind GeoIP2 / GeoLite2** If you prefer no external calls: 1. Download the **GeoLite2 City** database (CSV or binary). 2. Use the `geoip2` Python library to query: ```python import geoip2.database reader = geoip2.database.Reader('/path/to/GeoLite2-City.mmdb') response = reader.city('8.8.8.8') print(response.country.name, response.subdivisions.most_specific.name) ``` *Note:* MaxMind does **not** provide company contact info; you’ll need to map ASNs to companies manually (e.g., via the **RIPEstat** API). --- ## 5. Building your own wrapper API If you want a single endpoint that hides the provider details: ```python from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException import requests app = FastAPI() IPINFO_TOKEN = "YOUR_TOKEN" @app.get("/company/{ip}") def company_lookup(ip: str): url = f"https://ipinfo.io/{ip}/json" params = {"token": IPINFO_TOKEN} r = requests.get(url, params=params, timeout=5) if r.status_code != 200: raise HTTPException(status_code=r.status_code, detail=r.text) data = r.json() return { "ip": data.get("ip"), "company": data.get("org"), "city": data.get("city"), "region": data.get("region"), "country": data.get("country"), "postal": data.get("postal"), "location": data.get("loc"), # Add paid fields if present "phone": data.get("company", {}).get("phone"), "email": data.get("company", {}).get("email"), "website": data.get("company", {}).get("website"), } ``` Deploy with Docker, Uvicorn, or any cloud function platform. --- ## 6. Things to keep in mind | Topic | Recommendation | |-------|----------------| | **Rate limits** | Use caching (Redis, in‑memory) to avoid hitting the provider too often. | | **Error handling** | Return clear error codes (400 for bad IP, 429 for rate limit, 500 for provider failure). | | **Privacy** | Store only what you need; consider GDPR “right to be forgotten.” | | **Security** | Keep your API key secret; rotate it regularly. | | **Cost** | Estimate traffic; free tiers may be enough for low‑volume apps. | --- ### TL;DR 1. Pick a provider (ipinfo.io, ipapi.co, ipwhois.io). 2. Sign up → get an API key/token. 3. Call `GET https:////json?token=...` (or similar). 4. Parse the JSON; paid tiers expose `company.phone`, `company.email`, etc. 5. Wrap it in your own API if you want a single endpoint. Happy coding!
